scope: Apply the chara-action-state-pipeline / 0x00CF-moveactor-pipeline / 0x00D0-state-table-pipeline / 0x00CC-actor-record-apply Pattern B drill methodology to s2c 0x00D6 (and shared 0x00D7) - new rank 1 s2c gap (199 pcap hits) after 0x00CC's closure. Cases 0xD6/0xD7 have been enumerated as a fallthrough group with shared inner helper FUN_00586870 (BCS-Y-0622); the follow-up bit-state setters FUN_0058EBD0 + FUN_0058EBB0 were uncataloged. Drill to close the pipeline.

method.step1: Re-verify cases 0xD6/0xD7 fallthrough group: shared loop calls FUN_00586870(this, ushort idx, dword value) for N records (N = packet+0x90 for 0xD7, packet+0x110 for 0xD6 - different record-count offsets per opcode despite same handler). Follow-up sequence: FUN_0058EBD0(1) [bit-1 setter] + FUN_004D7980(0x46, ..., len) [scene-packet broadcast subtype 0x46] + FUN_004D73B0 [generic zone+0x4f4 getter, 47 callers] + FUN_00443E40(0, 0x1e, 7) [generic table lookup, 84 callers] + FUN_0058EBB0(prev_result) [bit-0 setter]. Main loop helper FUN_00586870 already cataloged BCS-Y-0622.
method.step2: Decomp FUN_0058EBD0 (32B): writes this+0xb20 = 1 (dirty flag) AND XOR-toggles bit 1 of this+0xb1c. Pattern: *(int*)(this+0xb1c) ^= ((param_2*2) ^ *(int*)(this+0xb1c)) & 2. This packs param_2's bit-0 into bit-1 of the state word.
method.step3: Decomp FUN_0058EBB0 (29B): writes this+0xb20 = 1 (dirty flag) AND XOR-toggles bit 0 of this+0xb1c. Pattern: *(int*)(this+0xb1c) ^= (*(int*)(this+0xb1c) ^ param_2) & 1. This packs param_2's bit-0 into bit-0 of the state word.
method.step4: Decomp FUN_004D73B0 (7B): returns *(int*)(param_1+0x4f4). Generic zone-state getter with 47 callers, NOT 0x00D6-specific.
method.step5: Decomp FUN_00443E40 (40B): returns *(int*)(*(int*)(param_1+8) + (param_2*0x20 + (param_3 & 0x1f))*0xbc + 0x60) OR param_4 fallback. Generic 0xbc-stride table lookup with 84+ callers, NOT 0x00D6-specific.
method.step6: Synthesize the cases 0xD6/0xD7 pipeline: arriving s2c 0x00D6 or 0x00D7 packet -> FUN_004DC690 top dispatcher -> CharaElement::vftable[9] = FUN_0058CCA0 case 0xD6/0xD7 fallthrough -> loop FUN_00586870 (BCS-Y-0622) populating actor+0xaac+i*4 table (max idx 0x1C) and setting actor+0xb20 dirty flag per record -> FUN_0058EBD0 (sets bit 1 of state word, sets dirty) -> FUN_004D7980(0x46) scene-packet broadcast -> generic getters (FUN_004D73B0 reads zone+0x4f4, FUN_00443E40 looks up entry by composite key) -> FUN_0058EBB0 (sets bit 0 of state word using prior lookup result, sets dirty).

key_findings: s2c 0x00D6 (new rank 1 s2c gap, 199 pcap hits) and s2c 0x00D7 share a fallthrough group handler. Per-opcode difference: record-count byte position - 0x00D7 reads count from packet+0x90, 0x00D6 reads from packet+0x110. Same per-record format (ushort idx + dword value), same target table (actor+0xaac+idx*4, max idx 0x1C = 28 records). Suggests 0x00D6 has a larger packet header (0x110 - 0x90 = 0x80 extra bytes preceding the count) - probably a 0x00D6 type-discriminator preamble that 0x00D7 lacks.

Target field layout (on Chara actor at this+0xaac region): 28-slot dword table at +0xaac..+0xb1c (0x70 bytes); state word at +0xb1c (bit 0 and bit 1 are independently togglable via FUN_0058EBB0/FUN_0058EBD0); dirty flag byte at +0xb20. This is a different region from 0x00D0_state_table_pipeline.json (which targets +0x188) and 0x00CC_actor_record_apply.json self-actor 16-slot (which targets +0x10c+4). The +0xaac region likely holds a different state class (combat parameters? cast progress? attribute snapshot?).

Two-bit composite state word at +0xb1c: FUN_0058EBD0 packs param_2's bit-0 into bit-1 (param_2*2 mask 2); FUN_0058EBB0 packs param_2's bit-0 into bit-0 (param_2 mask 1). Different XOR formulations achieve the same 'set bit N if param_2 bit-0 is set, else clear' semantic. Both set the +0xb20 dirty flag - any consumer can detect a 0x00D6/0xD7 update by polling that byte. Pattern suggests a 2-state event (e.g. 'casting started' bit AND 'cast interrupted' bit, or 'visible' bit AND 'targeted' bit).

Generic utility chain in 0xD6/0xD7 body: FUN_004D73B0 (7B getter for zone+0x4f4, 47 callers) and FUN_00443E40 (40B 0xbc-stride table lookup, 84+ callers) are NOT 0x00D6-specific. Both are pervasive engine utilities deferred from catalog. The FUN_00443E40 lookup uses composite key (param_2*0x20 + (param_3 & 0x1f)) * 0xbc + 0x60 = looks like a 32-entry-per-block * 0xbc-byte-per-entry table indexed by major/minor key.

Scene-packet subtype map (BCS-Y-0375/0376 framework): 0x00D6/0xD7 uses subtype 0x46 (distinct from 0x88=0x00D0, 0x26=0x00CF position, 0x34/0x35/0x36=0x00CF history snapshot, 0x39/0x3A=CharaBase _setPosition/_setDirection). 0x46 is the broadcast id for whatever combat/state event 0x00D6/0xD7 represents.

Methodology summary: Pattern B drill methodology now applied to 4 distinct routing variants - (a) FUN_0058CCA0 case body with cataloged helper [0x00D0]; (b) FUN_0058CCA0 case body needing leaf helper drill [0x00CE, 0x00CF]; (c) FUN_004D8860 fallthrough with cataloged branch heads needing Lua-side drill [0x00CC]; (d) FUN_0058CCA0 case body with cataloged main helper needing follow-up bit setters [0x00D6]. ALL 4 of the heaviest remaining Pattern B s2c gaps are now closed. Top of s2c gap list now drops to event-family/Pattern-E territory (0x0139, 0x0147, 0x00D2) which has different drill methodology.
